`01_qc_review` notebook has the kept/dropped numbers; here I just look at the cells before I
sign off

## The grid

Define function
```{python}
def _mk(c):
    s = jscatter.Scatter(data=df, x="x", y="y", height=340)
    if c in CAT:
        s.color(by=c, map=color_key(df, c))
    else:
        lo, hi = float(df[c].min()), float(df[c].max())
        s.color(by=c, map="magma", norm=[lo, hi if hi > lo else lo + 1e-9])
    s.legend(True)
    return s
```

Four linked panels — brush any one, the rest highlight the same cells. Colour by whatever,
edit `CHANNELS`, re-run.

```{python}
CAT = ["population_short", "tissue", "donor", "leiden_unsupervised"]

PANELS = [_mk(c) for c in CAT]
jscatter.compose([(s, c) for s, c in zip(PANELS, CAT)],
                 sync_view=True, sync_selection=True, sync_hover=True, rows=2)
```

```{python}
#| label: grid
CHANNELS = ["FOXP3", "pct_counts_mt", "score_eTreg", "CTLA4"]

PANELS = [_mk(c) for c in CHANNELS]
jscatter.compose([(s, c) for s, c in zip(PANELS, CHANNELS)],
                 sync_view=True, sync_selection=True, sync_hover=True, rows=2)
```

If lags, close panels 
```{python}
# close panels from a previous run (ipywidgets keeps every widget alive until closed)
for _s in globals().get("PANELS", []):
    try: _s.widget.close()
    except Exception: pass
```


I see high-mito effector like cluster of Tregs


## Characterise the selection

Save selection
```{python}
#| label: characterize
import pandas as pd
sel = first_selection(PANELS)
sub = df.iloc[sel]
print(sub)
```

```{python}
if len(sub) == 0:
    print("Lasso a cluster in the grid above, then re-run.")
else:
    print(f"{len(sub)} cells | SF {(sub.tissue=='synovial_fluid').mean():.0%} | "
          f"top donor {sub.donor.value_counts().idxmax()} ({sub.donor.value_counts(normalize=True).max():.0%})")
    cols = ["FOXP3", "CTLA4", "IL2RA", "pct_counts_mt", "n_genes_by_counts",
            "score_eTreg", "score_HSP", "score_apoptosis", "WT_heat_up"]
    display(pd.DataFrame({"selected": sub[cols].mean(),
                          "all_Treg": df[df.population_short == "Treg"][cols].mean()}).round(3))
```

Brushed tight, the FOXP3-hi / mt-hi pocket comes out ~99 % SF, CTLA4 high, FOXP3 a touch low, and high on the eTreg score. It seems to be an effector-Treg pocket — activated Tregs in the joint. Mostly
one donor (p6), so I hold it loosely.

## Channels

- `score_eTreg` — human effector-Treg signature (GSE161426, SF vs PB Treg; top genes CXCL13, CXCR6, EMP1, RCAN2). This is the one that tracks the pocket.
- `WT_heat_up` — the mouse 39 °C program. `score_KO_heat_up` and `score_Interaction_z` are the cGAS-KO and cGAS-dependent comparators, plus the 7 Interaction genes individually (IFI16, IRF7, MX1, …). The heat channels are quiet — nothing much stands out per cell.
- `score_HSP`, `score_apoptosis` — the stressed-vs-dying check; both flat in the pocket.

(`_up`/`_down`/`_updown`: each signature has an up- and down-set; `_up` scores the up-genes, `_updown` = up − down. `_up` is usually enough.)

## Save

jscatter's own save only grabs the points — no legend or labels. `save_selection` writes the barcodes (re-loadable later); `snapshot` writes a labelled figure. Both go to `eda/`.

```{python}
#| label: save
LABEL = "ctla4_pocket"                 # <- name it
sel = first_selection(PANELS)
save_selection(df, sel, label=LABEL)
snapshot(df, "score_eTreg", name=f"{LABEL}_eTreg", indices=sel)
```

```{python}
#| label: reload
import pandas as pd
saved = pd.read_csv("02_analysis/notebooks/01_qc_explore/eda/selection_sf_ctla4_pocket.csv", index_col=0)
sel_reloaded = df.index.get_indexer(saved.index)
sel_reloaded = sel_reloaded[sel_reloaded >= 0]
print(f"reloaded {len(sel_reloaded)} of {len(saved)} barcodes")
```
